{{recipe}}

'''Chicken cacciatore''' is a classic Italian chicken dish. It is reddish, and the tomato adds a distinct flavor.

==Ingredients==
* 1 ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (360 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]), [[cookbook:chop|chop]]ped [[cookbook:onion|onion]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]] (1350 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]), [[cookbook:chicken|chicken]] parts with skin removed
* 14 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (400 g) can of [[cookbook:tomato|tomato]]es with juice
* 5 ½ oz (155 g) can of [[cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 10 oz (280 g) can of [[cookbook:mushroom|mushroom]] pieces, drained
* 1 [[Cookbook:Bay leaf|bay leaf]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[cookbook:salt|salt]]
* ¼ tsp [[cookbook:pepper|pepper]]
* ¼ tsp [[cookbook:garlic powder|garlic powder]]
* 1 tsp dried whole [[cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
* ½ tsp dried [[cookbook:Basil|sweet basil]]
* ¼ cup (60 ml) of [[cookbook:White Wine|white wine]], chicken [[Cookbook:Broth|broth]], or alcohol-free white wine
* ½ tsp liquid gravy browner
* 1 tsp [[cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]

==Procedure==
# Place onion and chicken in 3 ½ [[Cookbook:Quart|quart]] (3.5 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]]) [[Cookbook:Slow Cooker|slow cooker]].
# Combine remaining ingredients in a bowl. Stir. 
# Pour over chicken and cover the chicken.
# Cook on low for 6–8 hours or on high for 3–4 hours.
# Discard bay leaf and serve.
